strategy_title: maxnreg Cap + Larger BLOCK_K Causes Register Spill Regression
strategy_description: Applying maxnreg=64 to cap register usage per thread (reducing registers/thread from 128 to 64) while simultaneously doubling BLOCK_K from 32 to 64 caused a ~2x slowdown (62us → 120us). Although registers/thread dropped as intended and Block Limit Registers improved (4→8), the larger shared memory footprint per block (32KB→65KB) became the new binding occupancy constraint, reducing Block Limit Shared Mem from 4 to 3 and lowering theoretical occupancy from 25% to 18.75%. Critically, the compiler spilled accumulator registers to local memory (new MemoryCacheAccessPattern rule: only 1/32 bytes utilized per sector for local loads/stores), generating massive uncoalesced local memory traffic that dominated execution time. The achieved occupancy remained unchanged at 6.25% despite the register reduction, confirming the shared memory limit became the new bottleneck. Do not apply maxnreg constraints when the resulting shared memory allocation (BLOCK_M * BLOCK_K * dtype_bytes + BLOCK_K * BLOCK_N * dtype_bytes) would reduce Block Limit Shared Mem below the current Block Limit Registers.
applicable_when: Never apply this combination: maxnreg cap that reduces registers/thread while simultaneously increasing BLOCK_K such that shared memory per block exceeds the previous shared memory limit.
do_not_apply_when: When increasing BLOCK_K causes shared memory per block to grow such that Block Limit Shared Mem becomes lower than the current Block Limit Registers — the shared memory becomes the new binding constraint and negates any register savings. Also avoid when the compiler responds to maxnreg by spilling accumulator registers to local memory (indicated by MemoryCacheAccessPattern rule triggering for local loads/stores with 1/32 byte utilization per sector).
framework_notes: In Triton, maxnreg in triton.Config() caps the PTX register count per thread. When the kernel has a large accumulator (e.g., BLOCK_M x BLOCK_N fp32 tile = 64*64*4 = 16KB of registers at 128 regs), forcing maxnreg=64 causes the compiler to spill the accumulator to local memory (L1TEX local space), generating strided uncoalesced accesses. The MemoryCacheAccessPattern NCU rule (local loads/stores with 1/32 byte sector utilization) is the diagnostic signal for this spill. Additionally, doubling BLOCK_K doubles the shared memory allocation, which can shift the binding occupancy constraint from registers to shared memory.

strategy_title: Switching tf32x3 to ieee Doubles Instructions and Regresses
strategy_description: Replacing input_precision='tf32x3' with input_precision='ieee' in tl.dot caused a 22% slowdown (71us → 76us). The ieee mode forces full FP32 FFMA execution, which more than doubled the executed instruction count (3.7M → 8.1M) and doubled registers per thread (64 → 128), making Block Limit Registers the new binding occupancy constraint (dropping from 8 to 4 blocks/SM). Simultaneously, removing maxnreg from autotune configs allowed the compiler to freely allocate 128 registers/thread, which shifted the shared memory limit (Block Limit Shared Mem went from 2 to 3) but the register limit became binding. The L2 hit rate also degraded significantly (95.63% → 70.92%) and severe shared memory bank conflicts emerged (12-way, 75% excessive wavefronts) that were not present before. The net effect is more instructions, more register pressure, and new bank conflicts — all causing regression despite the precision change being logically correct.
applicable_when: Never apply this combination: switching from tf32x3 to ieee precision while simultaneously removing maxnreg constraints, when tile sizes remain fixed at large values (BLOCK_M=BLOCK_N=BLOCK_K=64). The ieee mode requires more FP32 FFMA instructions and the compiler allocates more registers to hold intermediate values.
do_not_apply_when: When the kernel already uses maxnreg to cap register usage and tile sizes are large (BLOCK_M=BLOCK_N=64+): removing maxnreg while switching to ieee precision doubles instruction count and register pressure, making Block Limit Registers the new binding occupancy constraint. Also do not apply when the before-state already has Block Limit Shared Mem as the binding constraint (value=2) — the register increase from ieee mode will shift the binding constraint to registers and reduce theoretical occupancy.
framework_notes: In Triton, input_precision='tf32x3' uses three TF32 matmul passes to emulate FP32, which is faster but may introduce precision errors for large K. Switching to input_precision='ieee' forces full FP32 FFMA which is more accurate but generates significantly more instructions and higher register pressure. The maxnreg parameter in triton.Config() was previously capping registers at 64; removing it while switching to ieee allowed the compiler to allocate 128 registers/thread, doubling register pressure. The two changes (precision mode + maxnreg removal) must not be conflated — they have compounding negative effects on register-limited kernels.
